page: Amazon Web Services vt1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance specifically engineered for video transcoding and media processing workflows. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor delivering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory consists of 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by 8 Xilinx U30 media accelerators offering a collective 192 GB of video memory. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized throughput alongside modest per-core metrics. In synthetic workloads, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance reaches 80289.99 and PassMark CPU score records 53507.92, placing both in the top 25%. Software compilation via Clang achieves a score of 38983.0, and static web serving throughput measures 44.61 GB/sec. However, single-threaded processing reflects the lower clock profile, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1284.09 and Geekbench single-core at 1146.0, both situated in the bottom 25%. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 214.18 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth achieves 94.04 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides high density for multi-stream pipelines and multi-threaded processing. While the Intel CPU cores handle general compute tasks, the 8 Xilinx U30 accelerators are designed for ASIC-driven video transcoding rather than general-purpose GPGPU or large language model execution. This specialization is reflected in LLM text generation benchmarks, where generation speeds drop into the bottom 10% (31.9 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 5.2 tokens/sec on a 7B model). Workload efficiency is maximized when running live streaming ingestion, high-density video transcoding, and broadcast video pipelines that explicitly leverage the dedicated Xilinx U30 hardware.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via 8 Xilinx U30 media accelerators with 192 GB of total VRAM. The instance includes a 25 Gbps baseline network connection and contains no local storage.
